related_questions.question: How to fill in UK student visa application form?

text_blocks.snippet: To fill out a UK Student Visa application, you'll first need to create an account on the UK Visas & Immigration (UKVI) website. The application is completed online and you will need to pay the fee and book a biometric appointment. You'll need your passport, a Confirmation of Acceptance of Studies (CAS) number, and other supporting documents. Be sure to accurately enter all information, including personal details, passport information, and course details.
snippet_highlighted_words: create an account on the UK Visas & Immigration (UKVI) website

text_blocks.snippet: 1. Create an Account and Access the Application:

list.snippet: Go to the UKVI website and create an account.
Start a new application or continue a saved one.
Passport: Ensure your passport is valid and matches the details on your CAS.
CAS Number: This is a 14-digit number issued by your UK institution.
Supporting Documents: Have all required documents ready, including financial evidence, academic transcripts, and ATAS certificate (if applicable).
Personal Details: Have your personal information (name, date of birth, address, etc.) readily available.
Personal Information: Provide accurate details about yourself, including your name, date and place of birth, and contact information.
Passport Information: Enter your passport number, issuing authority, and expiry date.
Course Details: Enter the name of your course, your sponsor (university), and the start and end dates of your course.
Financial Information: Provide details about how you will be funding your studies.
Previous Visa Information: Answer truthfully about any previous visa applications or refusals.
Dependents: If you have dependents applying with you, you will need to provide their details and they will need to apply separately.
Biometrics: You will need to provide your fingerprints and a photograph (biometric information).
Payment: Pay the required visa application fee and the Immigration Health Surcharge (IHS).
Carefully review all your answers before submitting the application.
Once submitted, you will be directed to book a biometric appointment at a designated center.
Attend your appointment and provide your biometric information.
The UKVI will review your application and supporting documents.
You will receive an email notification regarding the outcome of your application.
Use the official UKVI website for the application form.
If you have any questions or need clarification, consult the resources provided by your university or the UKVI.
Do not submit your application until you have prepared all supporting documents.
Ensure all information is accurate and truthful to avoid delays or refusal of your application.

related_questions.question: How much bank balance is required for an UK student visa?

text_blocks.snippet: To get a UK student visa, you need to demonstrate you have enough money to cover your first year's tuition fees and living costs for up to 9 months. For living costs, you need £1,334 per month if studying in London and £1,023 per month if studying elsewhere in the UK. This money must be in your bank account for at least 28 consecutive days before applying.
snippet_highlighted_words: £1,334 per month if studying in London and £1,023 per month if studying elsewhere in the UK

list.title: Tuition Fees:
list.snippet: You need to show you have enough money to cover the first year's tuition fees, as stated on your Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS).
London: £1,334 per month for up to 9 months.
Outside London: £1,023 per month for up to 9 months.

list.title: Financial Evidence:
list.snippet: You can provide bank statements, a bank letter, or a sponsorship letter as proof of funds.

list.title: Dependents:
list.snippet: If you have dependents (spouse/partner or children), you'll need additional funds for them (e.g., £680 per month for each dependent outside London).

list.title: Age Requirement:
list.snippet: The age of the applicant does not affect the maintenance funds required, according to GOV.UK.

list.title: 28-Day Rule:
list.snippet: The funds must be held in your account for a minimum of 28 consecutive days before applying.

list.title: CAS:
list.snippet: The Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS) will specify the course fees you need to pay.

list.title: Not Relying on Future Income:
list.snippet: You cannot rely on future earnings (like part-time work) to meet the financial requirements.
